tldr: This paper presents "WorldSculpt," a method that reconstructs and generates hundreds of objects as individually manipulable, independent 3D meshes from videos of cluttered scenes with severe occlusions. By integrating a multi-view aggregation mechanism into a single-object 3D generative model, it achieves high-quality, editable compositional 3D worlds without any scene-level training.
hero_caption: Overall workflow of WorldSculpt. Given multi-view video and coarse 3D bounding boxes, an anchor-view-aligned canonical space (normalized coordinate frame) is defined for each object. Feature maps from multiple views are back-projected into a 3D voxel grid, aggregated, and injected into a 3D generative model (Pixal3D) to generate individual meshes, which are then placed back into the shared world frame.
overview:
Generative world models that synthesize expansive 3D environments from a single image or text prompt have advanced rapidly. However, existing models produce scenes as a single fused entity—either a unified mesh or a collection of 3D Gaussians—where individual objects like chairs and cups cannot be separated. This prevents robots from conducting physical simulations, such as picking up and moving a cup, and stops AR/VR systems from rearranging specific furniture pieces. Downstream tasks require a "compositional representation" where each object is treated as an independent mesh.

The authors hypothesized that by effectively adapting a high-precision single-object 3D generative prior, complex scenes with hundreds of densely packed objects could be recovered without any scene-level training. WorldSculpt builds upon an existing single-object 3D generative foundation model (Pixal3D) and adds a lightweight module that projects and aggregates multi-view image features into a shared 3D space. The model is trained exclusively on synthetic single-object data, with zero scene-level training data.

For evaluation, the authors created "UE-MeshyScene," a photorealistic benchmark built in Unreal Engine 5 containing densely cluttered scenes with up to 701 objects. Experimental results show that WorldSculpt significantly outperforms prior methods in geometric accuracy and placement precision under severe occlusions where objects are only partially visible. Furthermore, they demonstrate its practical value by automatically converting unified 3D Gaussian Splatting environments generated by other world models (such as Marble) into collections of individual, editable meshes.
contributions: Proposed WorldSculpt, a framework that directly generates editable 3D scenes composed of dozens to hundreds of independent object meshes from videos or multi-view images.
Designed an order-invariant multi-view conditioning mechanism that determines an optimal anchor view to establish a canonical space and geometrically lifts and aggregates multi-view DINOv3 features.

Demonstrated zero-shot generalization to densely occluded scenes without large-scale scene-level training, relying solely on LoRA fine-tuning and a curriculum data augmentation strategy on single objects.
Introduced UE-MeshyScene, a photorealistic benchmark featuring up to 701 objects under complex occlusions, complete with ground-truth meshes and per-object annotations.

sections.heading: From a Monolithic 3D Space to Individually Manipulable 3D Objects
sections.summary: Recent 3D world models generate high-quality scenes, but their fused monolithic representations prevent manipulating individual objects. Robotics and simulation require object-level separated meshes, which has been difficult to achieve in real cluttered scenes with heavy occlusion. This paper proposes a new paradigm that introduces multi-view conditioning into a powerful single-object 3D generative prior, turning hundreds of objects into individual meshes without any scene-level training.
sections.details:
Generative world models such as Marble and HY-World 2.0 can generate vast, navigable 3D environments from a single image. However, their output is a single fused mesh or cluster of Gaussians—what the authors describe as an "undifferentiated soup of surface geometry." From this representation, one cannot isolate a single chair or vase to feed into a physics simulator. For robotics and game development, decomposing scenes into individual mesh assets is an essential prerequisite.

Building compositional 3D representations from cluttered real-world scenes is a long-standing challenge. In dense environments, objects occlude one another, leaving each camera view with only a fraction of any given object's geometry.

Traditional geometry-based reconstructions (like NeRF and 3DGS) accurately capture visible surfaces, but leave occluded areas as empty holes. On the other hand, existing 3D generative models excel at synthesizing complete individual objects, but many take an unposed single image as input and struggle to align with absolute scene coordinate frames or multi-view constraints.

This is the key insight. The authors realized that by lifting multi-view observations into the canonical frame (an object-centric coordinate system) of a single object and aggregating them, they could leverage the shape completion capabilities of a strong single-object generative model without training on whole-scene data. WorldSculpt is the concrete realization of this idea.

sections.heading: The Missing Link Between Single-Object Generation and Scene Reconstruction
sections.summary: The paper provides a comprehensive overview of related work, including image-to-3D generation, amodal reconstruction for completing hidden geometry, and whole-scene generative models. It positions WorldSculpt as bridging the persistent gap between individual object generation and unified scene understanding.
sections.details:
Related work can be categorized into five main lines of research:

### 3D Generation from Images and Multi-View Inputs
Feed-forward models like LRM and InstantMesh, alongside native 3D generative models like Point-E, Shap-E, TRELLIS, and Pixal3D, have advanced rapidly. Because these are trained on clean single-object datasets such as Objaverse, applying them directly to complex real-world scenes is non-trivial.

### Amodal 3D Reconstruction
Amodal reconstruction aims to predict and restore the complete 3D shape of an object even when parts of it are occluded. Approaches include utilizing physical stability priors in robotics, 2D inpainting (pix2gestalt), and recent methods like Amodal3R. However, maintaining strict 3D consistency across multiple views remains challenging.

### Current State of 3D Datasets
Datasets like Toys4k and Google Scanned Objects provide clean single-object meshes without background context. In contrast, real-world datasets like CO3D and ScanNet feature objects merged into backgrounds, or only provide point clouds and bounding boxes without full ground-truth individual meshes.

### Scene-Level and Compositional Generation
Methods such as PartCrafter, MIDI, and SceneGen attempt to jointly predict object placements and shapes, but they remain restricted to simple scenes such as a tabletop with a few items.

### Structure from Motion and Video Understanding
Techniques for camera pose estimation (such as DUSt3R), open-world video segmentation (such as SAM 2/3), and 3D bounding box estimation have matured. WorldSculpt is designed as a practical pipeline that consumes outputs from these upstream tasks.

sections.heading: Lifting Multi-View Information to Canonical Voxels to Generate Individual Meshes
sections.summary: For each object in the scene, the method builds a canonical cube centered on the most visible anchor view and back-projects multi-view DINOv3 features into 3D voxels. An IBRNet-style aggregator pools features across arbitrary numbers of views, and LoRA layers inject them into a frozen Pixal3D model to synthesize accurate geometry while completing occluded parts.
sections.details:
The input consists of multi-view images with known camera poses, per-object 2D instance masks, and coarse 3D bounding boxes. The output is an individual mesh for each object along with a transformation matrix placing it in the world frame.

### 3.1 Anchor-Aligned Object Canonicalization
Coarse 3D bounding boxes often have irregular aspect ratios and arbitrary orientations. The framework selects the view where the object appears largest as the "anchor view" and establishes a cubic canonical volume $\mathcal{V}=[-0.5, 0.5]^3$ facing the anchor camera. The box is scaled isotropically to ensure the object stays within bounds across views. Changes in camera intrinsics caused by cropping and resizing view images are strictly tracked via mathematical formulation (Equations 6 and 7).

### 3.2 Multi-View Conditioned Object Generation
The 3D generator is based on Pixal3D (a Flow-Matching model built on TRELLIS.2), leveraging its Stage 1 (generating a coarse $64^3$ occupancy grid) and Stage 2 (generating high-resolution sparse structures).

- Feature Lifting: Cropped images are processed by DINOv3, and the resulting 2D feature maps are back-projected (sampled) to voxel coordinates within the canonical cube.
- View Aggregation: To handle a variable number of views without order dependence, an IBRNet-style lightweight MLP aggregates features at each voxel. It computes the mean and variance across views and adds an attention-weighted residual. The final layer of this residual block is zero-initialized, ensuring training begins smoothly from a simple mean.
- Condition Injection: The base weights of Pixal3D remain completely frozen. LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation, rank $r=32$) is applied solely to attention and projection layers to inject the 3D conditioning features.

### 3.3 Training and Curriculum Data Augmentation
Training relies exclusively on a synthetic single-object dataset (TexVerse). During training, anchor views are selected randomly, and the number of input views varies between 1 and 20. To handle real-world occlusions and noise, the authors introduce a curriculum that ramps up four types of corruptions over the first 3k steps: synthetic occlusion masks, camera pose perturbations, segmentation boundary noise, and resolution downsampling.

### 3.4 Inference and Scene Composition
During inference, meshes are generated independently for each object. Each reconstructed mesh is positioned into the scene's global world frame simply by applying the similarity transformation (rotation, translation, scale) computed during canonicalization. Because the system does not perform joint optimization over complex object-object interactions, it scales efficiently to parallel processing across hundreds of objects.

captions.F2: Detailed architecture of WorldSculpt. DINOv3 extracts features from multi-view images, which are lifted into a canonical voxel grid and aggregated via an IBR-style module. The aggregated features are injected into a frozen Pixal3D DiT block via zero-initialized projections and LoRA. The resulting canonical mesh is transformed back into the shared world frame.

sections.heading: Robust Recovery Without Failure, Even in Cluttered Scenes with Over 700 Objects
sections.summary: WorldSculpt was evaluated across three benchmarks: synthetic data (Toys4k, Toys4k-Scene), real-world data (HouseCat6D), and the newly created large-scale UE-MeshyScene. It significantly outperformed existing baselines in geometric fidelity and placement accuracy, especially in crowded environments with severe occlusions.
sections.details:
Evaluation metrics include Chamfer Distance (CD-$\ell_2$, CD-$\ell_1$), Earth Mover's Distance (EMD), and F-Score. For scene evaluations, the protocol compares directly against ground-truth meshes in the global world frame without per-object ICP alignment.

### The New Benchmark: "UE-MeshyScene"
Created in Unreal Engine 5.8, this benchmark features six large environments: Hangar, Ruins, Cathedral, Office, School, and Desert Town. Scenes contain between 93 and 701 objects, totaling 2,299 objects. The benchmark provides 5,964 camera trajectory viewpoints at $2560\times1440$ resolution, complete with ground-truth meshes, camera poses, instance masks, and depth maps.

### Key Experimental Findings
- Single Object (Toys4k): Performance improved consistently as the number of views increased from 1 to 16. Under an extreme setting with 75% occlusion, single-view baselines degraded sharply, whereas WorldSculpt maintained stable accuracy through multi-view feature aggregation.
- Scene Evaluation (Toys4k-Scene, HouseCat6D): The method was compared against state-of-the-art compositional generative baselines including SAM3D, SceneGen, SceneMaker, RecGen, and ShapeR. On real-world imagery (HouseCat6D), WorldSculpt generalized across the synthetic-to-real domain gap, recovering delicate shapes such as forks and shoes with high precision.
- Large-Scale Scenes (UE-MeshyScene): When evaluated against ShapeR, a strong multi-view baseline, WorldSculpt achieved clear advantages across both mean and median metrics (CD med). While ShapeR over-smoothed shapes or drifted in dense clusters, WorldSculpt cleanly reconstructed overlapping books, desks, and chairs as separated meshes.

### Ablation Studies and Applications
Comparing the learned IBR aggregator against a simple average (Avg) pooling baseline revealed that the learned module becomes increasingly superior as view counts and occlusion complexity grow (improving CD-$\ell_2$ by roughly 12% and F-Score from 0.944 to 0.951 on UE-MeshyScene).
In an application experiment, images were rendered along a virtual camera path from a 3D Gaussian Splatting scene generated by Marble. Using SAM 3 and DBSCAN clustering to detect bounding boxes, WorldSculpt converted the unified 3DGS environment into fully separated, high-quality individual meshes.

sections.heading: Summary and What Lies Ahead
sections.summary: WorldSculpt demonstrates that grounding a single-object 3D generative prior in multi-view observations makes it possible to build large compositional 3D worlds without scene-level training. The paper also outlines future research avenues, including texture synthesis and dynamic scenes.
sections.details:
The core of this work lies in combining single-object generative priors with multi-view geometric grounding. The finding that a model fine-tuned entirely on single-object data generalizes directly to real-world scale scenes where hundreds of objects occlude one another provides a scalable blueprint for 3D scene understanding and generation.

Experiments confirmed that as object counts rise and occlusions worsen, the advantage of this approach over pure geometric reconstructions and single-view generation widens.

Future work includes extending the generation process from pure geometry (meshes) to textures and physically based rendering (PBR) materials, as well as handling dynamic scenes where humans or robots move and interact with objects.

takeaways: Without whole-scene training, a strong single-object 3D generative model augmented with a multi-view geometric aggregation module can scale zero-shot to massive compositional scenes.

Constructing a canonical cube aligned to the best-visibility anchor view, lifting image features to 3D voxels, and aggregating them via an IBRNet-style module yields strong robustness against occlusion.
A curriculum data augmentation strategy that progressively intensifies occlusions, camera noise, and mask artifacts during training significantly improves resilience to real-world noise.
Outputs from 3D Gaussian generative world models (such as Marble) can be post-processed into simulation-ready individual meshes when paired with tools like SAM 3.
limitations: The system depends on the accuracy of upstream camera pose estimation, 2D instance segmentation masks, and coarse 3D bounding boxes; severe mask errors or bounding box misalignments degrade output quality.
The current model is limited to generating 3D geometry (meshes) and does not synthesize object colors or textures (PBR materials), leaving texture generation for future work.
The approach assumes static environments and cannot handle dynamic objects that move or deform during observation.
